articles.title: Syria: Humanitarian Situation Monitoring (HSM), November 2026 [EN/AR]
articles.description: Please refer to the attached files. KEY MESSAGES • Livelihoods (68%) and food (66%) emerged as the two leading priority needs reported by KIs in assessed communities, largely driven by rising living costs. Nearly two-thirds of KIs (65%) reported substantial increases in living costs, while 94% of those reporting food-related difficulties cited the inability to afford food or associated fuel and transportation costs. • Winterisation was the third most frequently reported priority need (53%), with rising heating fuel costs and inadequate electricity availability compounding seasonal vulnerabilities and increasing the risk that households will be forced to divert limited resources from food and other essential needs to maintain adequate warmth during winter. • Rising fuel prices acted as a multi-sectoral crisis multiplier, driving up the costs of food, transportation, heating, agricultural production and essential services, with 92% of KIs identifying fuel price increases as a key driver of rising household costs. • Deir-ez-Zor, Al-Hasakeh and Dar’a emerged as key areas of concern. In Deir-ez-Zor, livelihood deterioration and winterisation needs overlapped with food unaffordability and WASH and healthcare gaps; in Al-Hasakeh, severe food insecurity, winterisation pressures and limited access to essential services were compounded by declining purchasing power; while Dar’a faced overlapping water, shelter, livelihood and healthcare challenges.
